headline: Media firms see revenue growth but tighten costs, while gaming, publishing and education show mixed performance and technology focus.
summary: Disney and WBD posted revenue gains but are cutting costs aggressively. Gaming shows a split with Caesars losing money and Bally's expanding. Publishing has strong AI and acquisition activity but Scholastic missed revenue. Education is divided between Pearson's growth and SLU's staff cuts. Across all sectors, IT spending is under pressure with selective expansion in digital and AI initiatives.

industries.summary: Revenue grew double‑digits for Disney and WBD, while Versant added streaming channels. Cost‑cutting is a major theme, with $3 bn savings targeted at Disney and $6 bn at WBD. AI and platform rebuilds are being pursued despite tighter budgets.

laggards.why: Operating margin only 5.2% and revenue growth slowing

themes.title: Cost cutting
themes.detail: Disney aims for $3 bn savings by 2029; WBD plans $6 bn annual cuts after its merger.

themes.title: AI & tech investment
themes.detail: Both Disney and WBD mention AI use in parks and future tech initiatives.

themes.title: Digital platform expansion
themes.detail: Versant launched new FAST channels and a streaming membership.

industries.it_note: IT budgets are being trimmed even as companies invest in AI and streaming platforms.

industries.summary: Caesars posted a $123 m loss despite modest revenue growth. Bally's saw 22% revenue growth and is expanding tech. Light & Wonder and Brightstar focus on cost reduction and new lottery tech.

themes.title: Digital revenue growth
themes.detail: Bally's and Caesars both reported digital revenue increases, with Bally's seeing strong interactive segment growth.

themes.title: Cost‑cutting pressure
themes.detail: Light & Wonder targets debt reduction; Caesars tightens spending while questioning AI's role.

themes.title: New lottery technology
themes.detail: Brightstar unveiled next‑gen lottery solutions and secured a multi‑year contract in Spain.

industries.it_note: Spending is constrained, but firms continue to fund digital platforms and selective automation.

industries.summary: Wolters Kluwer is expanding through acquisitions and AI partnerships. Scholastic missed revenue and posted a large operating loss. Pearson delivered strong revenue growth and AI credential expansion.

leaders.why: Revenue of $1,779 m and improving operating margin

laggards.why: Revenue miss of $216.8 m and operating loss of -42.5%

themes.title: AI integration
themes.detail: Wolters Kluwer partners with Viz.ai; Pearson expands AI credentials on Credly.

themes.title: M&A activity
themes.detail: Wolters Kluwer acquires AgileMD for up to $100 m.

themes.title: Cost restructuring
themes.detail: Pearson announced a major business restructure to improve margins.

industries.it_note: Investments in AI and platform capabilities are outpacing overall cost‑cutting measures.

industries.summary: Pearson continues revenue acceleration and AI credential growth. SLU cuts staff and outsources custodial services, indicating tightening. NYU pilots a shuttle‑bus program and proposes accelerated degrees, while ACT reports mixed test trends.

leaders.why: Revenue growth and expanding AI credential program

themes.title: AI credential expansion
themes.detail: Pearson's Credly platform saw a 506% rise in AI credentials over two years.

themes.title: Outsourcing and staff cuts
themes.detail: SLU moves custodial services to an external provider; broader cost tightening.

themes.title: Program innovation
themes.detail: NYU pilots shuttle‑bus service and proposes three‑year bachelor degrees.

industries.it_note: Pearson expands tech spend, while SLU tightens budgets; overall IT direction varies by institution.
